issues.detail: The skill is tied to Burp Suite's Java-based GUI workflow (Proxy, Repeater, Intruder, Scanner tabs, BApp Store extensions), which is not something a non-interactive AI agent can drive directly without a human operating the GUI.

scenarios.name: idor-order-enumeration
scenarios.rationale: Both cover Repeater manual ID swap and Intruder with §id§ injection point sweeping a numeric range filtered by status/length to measure exposure, with comparable completeness and specificity.

scenarios.name: jwt-privilege-escalation-check
scenarios.rationale: A covers the full rubric (proxy/capture, Repeater, token swap, 200 OK check, Autorize, JWT Editor mention) with more depth, while B covers Repeater/token-swap/200/Autorize but was truncated by a safety classifier before completing the response and never mentions JWT Editor or explicit interception of the member's own request.

scenarios.name: hidden-param-discovery-before-fuzzing
scenarios.rationale: Response B correctly recommends Param Miner from the BApp Store, right-clicking to guess params, and confirming in Repeater before Intruder, fully matching the rubric, while Response A refuses and offers unrelated alternatives, not addressing the rubric at all.
